scope: Six supporting-lemma study targets spanning six published families. No claim of novel or open-problem solutions.

targets.title: Exact-length Egyptian fractions and marker-preserving padding
targets.statement: For an integer k≥1, if 0<x<1 is a sum of exactly k positive integer-denominator unit fractions, then x has an exactly-k-term expansion with pairwise distinct integer denominators, all ≥2. Companion: if 1=Σ(i=1..r)1/n_i with 2≤n_1<⋯<n_r and r≥3, any chosen denominator m among the n_i can be retained in a distinct exactly-(r+1)-term expansion of 1.
targets.source_locator: elementary.tex, Lemma lem:distinct; prescribed.tex, Lemma lem:exact-marker-padding
prerequisites: Induction and finite sorted denominator lists
Elementary divisibility and prime/composite cases
Well-founded termination via a finite-state increasing potential
targets.deliverable: Independent proof, exact rational tests, a terminating rewrite specification, and boundary/collision cases including x=1 and a marked largest denominator.
targets.reusable_bridge: Number theory ↔ finite combinatorial rewriting and termination.
targets.headline_boundary: Does not establish the manuscript's O(log log b) upper bound; these lemmas are classical/attributed supporting results.
targets.lean_scope: Family025 scope lists short expansion, counting, and prescribed-denominator statements. Not compiled or matched to the individual lemma in this run.

targets.title: Normalized periodic hitting implies global affine avoidance
targets.statement: Fix q∈(0,1). Suppose for each p∈(0,1) there exists open 1-periodic H⊂R, of density ρ(H)≤6p, such that every x∈R and t∈[1,2] has x+tq^n∈H for some n≥1. Then for every η∈(0,1) there exists compact E⊂[0,1] with m(E)>1−η and, for every x∈R and s≠0, some n≥1 satisfies x+sq^n∉E. The source uses p_k=(η/64)4^{−|k|}, C=⋃(k∈Z)(2^kH_k∪−2^kH_k), and m(C∩[0,1])≤7η/16.
targets.source_locator: 02-periodic.tex, proof of main theorem assuming Proposition prop:periodic
prerequisites: Lebesgue measure and countable subadditivity
Periodic density under dilation
Dyadic normalization of a nonzero real scale
Compactness of a closed subset of [0,1]
targets.deliverable: Independent proof and generalized reduction for a prescribed null sequence or scale family, with explicit summable budgets. Keep construction of normalized hitting sets as a hypothesis.
targets.reusable_bridge: Analysis ↔ topology: measure budgeting, periodicity, and compact complements.
targets.headline_boundary: Only the reduction is studied; existence of normalized hitting sets is a major separate premise.
targets.lean_scope: Family084 Lean note covers only the September25 dyadic manuscript q=1/2, not this October5 arbitrary-q manuscript.

targets.title: Radial contact in normed balls
targets.statement: Let X be a nonzero real normed space and ||c||<1. For every v∈S_X, the ray c+R_+v meets S_X at a unique c+ρ(v)v, with 1−||c||≤ρ(v)≤1+||c||. The radius function ρ:S_X→(0,∞) is continuous.
targets.source_locator: main.tex, Lemma lem:radial; supporting-functionals Lemma lem:support
prerequisites: Norm convexity and triangle inequality
One-dimensional intermediate value arguments
Supporting functionals for a quantitative extension
targets.deliverable: Independent proof, a quantitative modulus/Lipschitz bound with explicit dependence on distance of c to the boundary, and examples showing why the interior hypothesis matters.
targets.reusable_bridge: Topology of radial parametrizations ↔ convexity and Banach-space inequalities.
targets.headline_boundary: No general Tingley extension theorem or alignment proposition is assumed or certified.
targets.lean_scope: Family322 claims a unique real-linear extension for arbitrary nonzero real Banach spaces; the scope is real, not complex linearity. No Lean run performed.

targets.title: Three-atom transport obstruction with exact distances
targets.statement: Let d≥2, ρ be uniform on [-1,1]^d, 0<a<1/2 and b=a/2. Put u_a=max{−x_1,x_1,a} and v_a=max{−x_1,x_1,a+bx_2}. Their gradient laws are μ_a=((1−a)/2)(δ_{−e1}+δ_{e1})+aδ_0 and ν_a=((1−a)/2)(δ_{−e1}+δ_{e1})+aδ_{be2}. The gradients are the unique quadratic optimal maps to their laws, W_2(μ_a,ν_a)^2=ab², W_1(μ_a,ν_a)=ab, and ||T_μa−T_νa||²_L2(ρ)=b/2+ab². Hence no uniform estimate with exponent α>1/3 can hold on this fixed source and target cube, even for three-atom targets.

prerequisites: Finite maxima of affine functions and null hyperplanes

targets.reusable_bridge: Convex analysis ↔ probability, optimal transport, and sharp Hölder exponents.
targets.headline_boundary: The explicit lower-bound obstruction is independent of the claimed uniform global upper bound.

targets.title: Mixed moments and Taylor-contact cancellation
targets.statement: For nonnegative integers i,j define M(i,j)=∫_{−1}^1∫_0^1 [|t|/√(1−t²)]t^i s^j/(1−ts) ds dt and Z(i,j)=∫_0^1∫_0^1 t^i s^j/(1−ts) ds dt. Extend bilinearly to polynomials. Let G=Σ(j≥0)(−1)^j/(2j+1)². If P,D∈Q[t], L≥1 is an integer and tP(t)/√(1−t²)−D(t)=O(t^L) at t=0, then for every integer 0≤j<L, M(P,j)−(3/2)Z(D,j) belongs to Q+QG. Supporting identity: Z(i,i)=ζ(2)−H_i^(2), while Z(i,j)=(H_i−H_j)/(i−j) for i≠j.
targets.source_locator: foundations.tex, equations rational-decomposition and contact; Proposition prop:rationality (the polynomial-generalized lemma is an extraction)
prerequisites: Absolute convergence and justified termwise integration
Beta-type moments and central binomial coefficients
Rational recurrences and harmonic numbers
Taylor coefficient matching
targets.deliverable: Verify mixed-moment recurrences and the two boundary constants, then prove the general cancellation lemma. Exact rational low-index checks may detect indexing errors; keep G symbolic.
targets.reusable_bridge: Real analysis ↔ rational arithmetic, special functions, and symbolic elimination.
targets.headline_boundary: This is not a proof of Catalan's irrationality. The determinant, valuation, nonvanishing and energy arguments remain outside the study.
targets.lean_scope: Family005 scope claims irrationality of Catalan's constant. The extracted generalized cancellation lemma has not been identified as a formal declaration here.

targets.title: Positive-block energy and convex outer approximation
targets.statement: Primary lemma: if Δ=[[A,B],[B*,C]] is a finite complex positive-semidefinite block matrix, then 2||B||²_HS≤||A||²_HS+||C||²_HS. Scaling gives the stronger product bound ||B||²_HS≤||A||_HS||C||_HS. Companion target: every nonempty compact convex K⊂C has bounded open convex real-analytic Jordan neighborhoods Ω_δ with K⊂Ω_δ and sup(z∈closure Ω_δ)dist(z,K)≤δ(1+diam K)/(1−δ), for 0<δ<1, via finite direction nets and a log-sum-exp support barrier.
targets.source_locator: main.tex, section sec:matrix, 'The positive block comparison'; Lemma lem:approx and its proof
prerequisites: Positive-semidefinite matrices, trace cyclicity and Hilbert–Schmidt norm
Congruence and one-variable optimization for the product bound
For the companion: support functions, finite sphere nets, convexity and the implicit function theorem
targets.deliverable: Independent block-inequality proof with dimension-independent constants and equality/zero-block checks. Optionally extract the outer-approximation argument as a reusable planar topology/analysis lemma.
targets.reusable_bridge: Matrix inequalities ↔ noncommutative analysis; convex geometry ↔ smooth approximation.
targets.headline_boundary: Neither supporting lemma establishes the complete Crouzeix constant-two theorem.
